description: Cross-endpoint replay defense for the v0.5 `response` entry (§9.8): the signed context binds `to` — the session-qualified address the entry is delivered to — but the §6 body carries no `to`, so the binding only holds because the verifier reconstructs `to` from its OWN presented drain identity. The honest control (entry verified at the session it was signed for, sess_01J5OVR0001) MUST pass first. Replayed unmodified to a DIFFERENT session of the same principal (sess_01J5OVR0002 — the sharpest case: same credential, same agent.id), the reconstructed context diverges and verification MUST fail with a signature mismatch. A payload tamper (response.value flipped) likewise diverges the recomputed §9.2 digest, and a correlation rebind (in_reply_to flipped to another live ask) diverges the reconstructed `id`/`in_reply_to` pair — the response-side analogue of dp-017's receipt rebind.
obligation: Verify the honest control at drain identity agent:overseer/fleet#sess_01J5OVR0001; then (1) reject the SAME entry + header verified at drain identity agent:overseer/fleet#sess_01J5OVR0002 (reconstructed `to` diverges — cross-session replay), (2) reject the tampered entry (response.value approve->deny; recomputed payload_sha256 diverges) at the honest identity, and (3) reject the rebound entry (in_reply_to flipped to a different live ask; the reconstructed `id` := in_reply_to diverges with it, so a real approval cannot be misdirected onto another ask) at the honest identity — all with a signature mismatch, not a window/jti rejection. Expected runner wiring (#26): mirror the dp-003/dp-006 branch — reconstruct the context per case (verifier-supplied `to`, recomputed digest, entry's in_reply_to as `id`) and verify against `v1`.

tampered_entries.reason: answer tamper — response.value flipped approve->deny in transit; the verifier recomputes the §9.2 digest from the payload it received, so the flipped answer diverges payload_sha256

correlation rebind — in_reply_to flipped to a different live ask of the same submitter: the verifier reconstructs `id` from the received in_reply_to, so both bound fields diverge and a genuine approval cannot be misdirected onto another ask
